title: Crostini con Fegatini
subtitle: Chicken liver pâté on toasted bread, Tuscan style
excerpt: Crostini con fegatini is a Tuscan antipasto: toasted or grilled small bread rounds spread with a smooth, savoury chicken liver pâté cooked with onion, capers, and anchovies. The spread is dark, rich, and savoury. It is one of the most important antipasto preparations in Tuscany and appears on almost every table before a meal.
sourceNotes: Crostini neri (black crostini) with chicken livers is a signature Tuscan preparation. Artusi, La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene (1891), public domain, includes chicken liver crostini preparations. The dish is documented in Pellegrino Artusi and remains the most common antipasto preparation in Tuscan homes and restaurants.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The chicken liver spread keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Toast the bread just before serving.

glossaryTerms.definition: Italian for chicken livers (singular: fegatino). Used in the Tuscan antipasto crostini neri, where the livers are cooked with aromatics and spread onto toasted bread rounds.

content.text: is the classic Tuscan antipasto that opens almost every formal meal in the region. Chicken livers are cooked with onion, then flavoured with capers, anchovy fillets, and a splash of vin santo or white wine before being chopped or blended to a rough, spreadable consistency. It is intensely savoury and rich: a small amount goes far.

items.prepNote: trimmed of sinew and any green bits

content.text: Heat {{olive-oil}} of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Add the {{onion}} of diced onion and cook for 6 minutes until soft. Add the {{anchovies}} of anchovies and {{sage}} sage leaves; stir until the anchovies have melted into the oil.

Increase the heat to medium-high and add the {{chicken-livers}} of trimmed chicken livers. Cook, turning, for 3 to 4 minutes until browned on the outside but still slightly pink inside. Add {{white-wine-dry}} of white wine or vin santo and the {{capers}} of rinsed capers and let it bubble for 2 minutes until the wine has mostly evaporated.

Remove the sage leaves. Transfer everything to a board and chop finely with a knife, or pulse a few times in a food processor, until the mixture is a rough, spreadable paste. It should have some texture rather than being completely smooth. Season with {{salt-table}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Cool for 30 minutes before spreading.
Toast the {{baguette}} bread rounds under the grill or on a ridged griddle pan until golden. Spread each round generously with the chicken liver mixture and serve immediately.

items.cause: The green bile ducts were not fully trimmed from the livers, or they were overcooked.
items.fix: Inspect each liver carefully and cut away any green or dark yellow parts before cooking. Cook to still-pink inside , overcooked livers become grainy and bitter.

items.cause: The livers were overcooked, making them dry, or the mixture was over-processed.
items.fix: Aim for a just-pink centre in the livers. Chop by hand or pulse briefly; the texture should be rough and spreadable, not a smooth mousse.

content.text: Crostini neri di fegatini is the signature antipasto of Tuscany, particularly of Florence and the surrounding countryside. In Tuscan homes, a board of mixed crostini is the expected start to a Sunday lunch or celebration meal: chicken liver, white bean, and other toppings on small rounds of toasted bread. The liver version is almost always included. Outside Italy, chicken liver pâté is better known in a French style (smooth and cream-enriched). The Tuscan version is drier, coarser, and more intensely savoury.
